The architecture

One canvas, grown by bands. Band 1 is the analyze pulse — the only path that writes, and the one every other command reads the output of. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, click a block to trace its wiring, double-click or use the i to open its page.

click to highlight · double-click or the i to open · click an edge to trace it · Esc clears 100%

What this band does NOT show

A boundary is not completeness (rules.md §11). Band 1 draws the write path through the four core features it crosses. It does not show:

  • The 35 read commands. Every one of them reads what this band produced — query, impact, trace, audit, prune — and none is drawn here. That is a future band, not an omission of this one.
  • The MCP surface. Fourteen tools sit beside the CLI over the same registry.
  • The other five core features. contracts, utils, algorithms, registry and bootstrap are crossed by this path but are not stages in it; each has a module note instead.
  • The watcher. An incremental pulse re-enters this band mid-way rather than at the top, and drawing that edge honestly needs the read band to exist first.

Read log

Every block on this canvas was written from a file opened during the ADR 0150 core campaign, not from memory — the rule that produced five corrected claims on the repo this standard came from. The derived list below is generated from the anchors themselves.

Read at d184968 — the campaign's own log, docs/deep_clean.md, records what was measured at each step and what each measurement cost.

A visual is traced at a moment and starts rotting immediately. Anchors are checked by conducks visuals-lint; the layout is computed by ELK and verified by a collision gate that refuses to emit an overlapping picture. Neither reads prose — that an anchor resolves is not evidence the sentence attached to it is still true.
